newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Italy urges Belgrade to accept opposition win.
newsitem.headline: Italy urges Belgrade to accept opposition win.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini urged Serbian authorities on Tuesday to recognise opposition victories in municipal polls or risk an escalation in their conflict with protesters.

Dini said the opposition coalition, which has staged nine weeks of mass demonstrations to demand restoration of its win in November's elections, had promised the European Union to halt the protests if Belgrade recognised the poll results.

An inquiry by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) verified the opposition's claim to have won Belgrade and 13 other towns where the Socialists annulled election results claiming "irregularities".

"If progress -- reinstatement -- is not made in this direction rapidly, an intensification of demonstrations awaits us -- a blockage of roads that could thus prevent normal economic life," Dini told a news conference in Geneva.
"An escalation of conflict should be avoided," he added.

"We have assurances and commitments from opposition members that once this (reinstatement) happens, they will stop all demonstrations and are ready to sit together around the table of dialogue with representatives of other parties," Dini said.

While stressing the need to keep the dialogue open with the Belgrade government, Dini said the European Union's 15 member states were in full agreement over the need for Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic to accept the election results.
"There is complete agreement among all members of the EU that the government of Milosevic has to accept the conclusions and recommendations of the mission by Gonzales," Dini said.
The EU on Monday expressed full support for the opposition coalition and demanded the Belgrade authorities recognise its election victories.
Western governments have told Milosevic to forget about economic reconstruction aid unless his government admits the poll losses.
